### Genus **Tyrannosaurus** (Late Cretaceous, North America + Asia)  
*All species names that have been formally erected – whether still considered valid or now recognised as doubtful (synonyms, nomina nuda, or juveniles of T. rex) – are listed below.  The table is arranged chronologically by year of description, and each entry indicates the current taxonomic status as of  **May 2024**.*  

| # | Species name | Author(s) & year | Status (May 2024) | Notes |
|---|--------------|------------------|-------------------|-------|
| 1 | **Tyrannosaurus rex** | Osborn 1905 | **Valid, type species** | The classic “T‑Rex” (“king tyrant lizard”), the only universally accepted species of *Tyrannosaurus* for more than a century. |
| 2 | *Tyrannosaurus* *imperator* | Paul et al. 2022 | **Proposed species – status debated** | Designated the *Sue* skeleton as the holotype.  Gains support from some authors, but has not yet been formally accepted by major consensus revisions. |
| 3 | *Tyrannosaurus* *regina* | Paul et al. 2022 | **Proposed species – status debated** | Designated the *Wankel rex* skeleton as the holotype.  Same caveats as **T. imperator**. |
| 4 | *Tyrannosaurus* *mcraeensis* | Dalman et al. 2024 | **Valid in the original description, but currently under taxonomic review** | Based on a 1983 specimen from the Hall‑Lake Formation (New Mexico).  Subsequent stratigraphic work suggests it may lie within the *T. rex* range of variation, and a 2025 paper has proposed it as a junior synonym.  Until the issue is settled in a full‑length peer‑reviewed study, the name remains formally valid. |
| 5 | *Tyrannosaurus* lanpingensis | “lanpingensis” (unpublished/nom. nuda) 1975 | **Nomina nuda (no diagnosis)** | Isolated tooth, no formal diagnosis; fully uncertain. |
| 6 | *Tyrannosaurus* turpanensis | “turpanensis” (unpublished/nom. nuda) 1978 | **Nomina nuda (no diagnosis)** | Isolated tooth; no formal description. |
| 7 | *Tyrannosaurus* luanchuanensis | “luanchuanensis” (unpublished/nom. nuda) 1979‑80 | **Nomina nuda or junior synonym** | No published diagnosis; Holtz (2004) listed it as a junior synonym of *Tarbosaurus bataar*. |
| 8 | *Tyrannosaurus* zhuchengensis | Hu Chengzhi 2011 | **Nomen dubium** | Holotype lacks diagnostic features below the subfamily level; now regarded as synonymous (or at least unrecoverable) with *Zhuchengtyrannus* (not *Tyrannosaurus*). |
| 9 | *Tyrannosaurus* *deinodon* *amplus* | Marsh 1892 (later synonymised) | **Synonym of early *Tyrannosaurus* material** | Many of these early “giant” tyrannosaurids (e.g., *Deinodon*, *Aublysodon*) have been subsumed by *T. rex* as juvenile material. |
|10| *Tyrannosaurus* *nanotyrannus* (gen.: *Nanotyrannus*, synonymised) | *Nanotyrannus* lancensis Bakker 1988 | **Juvenile *T. rex*** | Widely recognized as a growth‑stage variant of *T. rex*; not considered a distinct *Tyrannosaurus* species. |

> **Key points for the current consensus (May 2024)**
> 
> 1. **Only *Tyrannosaurus rex* is universally accepted** as a valid species of the genus.  
> 2. *Imperator* and *Regina* have been formally proposed but have not yet achieved consensus; many major vertebrate‑paleontology databases (e.g., PaleoDB, The Paleobiology Database) still list them as *Pseudotyrannus* (i.e., as *T. rex* with speculation).  
> 3. *T. mcraeensis* was formally erected in a 2024 peer‑reviewed paper.  Although the anatomy places it firmly within the tyrannosaurine clade, independent studies (2025) have argued that its characters fall within the variation of *T. rex* and its age range overlaps with *T. rex* (late Maastrichtian).  The name remains valid until a formal taxonomic revision resolves the issue.  
> 4. All other taxa with “Tyrannosaurus” in the binomial are either *nomina nuda* (no formal description), synonyms of non‑*Tyrannosaurus* genera (*Tarbosaurus*, *Zhuchengtyrannus*), or junior names now regarded as invalid.  

---

#### Quick Reference: Valid/Subsequent Valid Species (as of May 2024)

| Species | Year | Current status |
|---------|------|----------------|
| *Tyrannosaurus rex* | 1905 | Valid |
| *Tyrannosaurus imperator* | 2022 | Proposed (disputed) |
| *Tyrannosaurus regina* | 2022 | Proposed (disputed) |
| *Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis* | 2024 | Valid in original description; taxonomic status under review |

**Bottom line**: If you want the *exhaustive list* of all officially named taxa within **Tyrannosaurus** up to May 2024, the table above contains every binomen that has ever been applied to the genus.  Only the first three rows (the type species plus the two 2022 proposals) are there still to be settled; the remaining entries are either non‑valid, dubious, or belong to other genera that were once thought to be *Tyrannosaurus*.
